title: Beeswax & dried orange peel pillar candle
subtitle: A freestanding beeswax pillar with a warm citrus note
excerpt: A hand-dipped or moulded beeswax pillar candle with dried sweet orange peel embedded in the surface for a gentle festive look. Beeswax burns cleaner and longer than paraffin or soy, with its own faint honey-wax scent. Makes one 200 g pillar; burns for around 20 hours.
sourceNotes: Pillar candle method: beeswax melts at 62-65°C; pour temperature 70-75°C for pillar moulds to prevent air bubbles. Wick sizing for beeswax pillars: square-braided wicks designed for beeswax; the thicker beeswax requires a larger wick than the same-diameter soy candle. Dried orange peel: slice thinly, dry in oven at lowest setting for 2 hours; press gently into the surface of the candle while the outer wax is still slightly tacky after unmoulding.

recipe.yieldDescription: 1 pillar candle (~200 g, approx. 6 cm diameter × 8 cm tall; ~20-hour burn time)
recipe.batchNotes: Doubles cleanly if you have multiple pillar moulds. Pour all in the same session, beeswax sets quickly once below 60°C and needs to be poured while still hot.
recipe.makeAheadNotes: Beeswax pillar candles improve with a short cure, the wax hardens and the scent becomes more even after a few days. Make at least 3 days before use.
recipe.shelfLifeNotes: Beeswax candles last indefinitely; the wax does not deteriorate. A white bloom (called bloom) may develop on the surface over time, this is natural wax crystallisation, harmless, and can be buffed off with a soft cloth.

glossaryTerms.definition: The temperature at which melted wax is poured into the mould. For beeswax pillar candles, 70°C gives a clean fill with minimal air bubbles; pouring cooler can leave voids inside the pillar.

When a pillar candle burns straight down through the centre without melting the outer wax wall. Usually caused by an undersized wick for the candle's diameter. The remedy is a larger wick on the next batch.

content.text: A beeswax pillar with dried orange peel pressed into the surface is a warm, freestanding candle that suits a table or mantelpiece. Beeswax burns cleaner and longer than paraffin or soy, with its own faint honey-sweet scent that pairs naturally with the citrus of the orange peel. The pillar holds its shape as it burns; there is no jar to manage. One 200 g pillar; burns for around 20 hours.

items.prepNote: yellow cosmetic-grade beeswax pastilles or grated block; beeswax needs no added fragrance
square-braided beeswax wick sized for 6 cm diameter pillar; cut to mould height plus 5 cm
thin-sliced dried sweet orange peel for surface decoration; press into wax before final set

content.text: Thread the wick through the base hole of the pillar mould and pull taut. Seal the base hole with a wick tab or a small ball of Blu-Tack. Loop the top of the wick over a pencil laid across the mould rim to keep it centred.

Melt the beeswax in the pouring pitcher over a simmering-water bath, watching the temperature. Never leave melting wax unattended, beeswax above its flash point (around 250°C) catches fire. Keep a fire blanket nearby. Bring to 75°C.
for pillar beeswax. Pour slowly into the mould to avoid air bubbles.
As the wax cools it contracts slightly and may sink around the wick. Top up with a small pour of wax at the same temperature after 30 minutes.
Leave to set at room temperature for 24 hours. Unmould by inverting and tapping, the pillar should slide out. If the mould is metal, place it in the fridge for 10 minutes to shrink the wax slightly.
While the outer surface is still very slightly tacky (about 10 minutes after unmoulding), press the dried orange peel slices gently into the outer surface. They will embed as the wax fully sets.
Trim the wick to 5 mm before lighting. Watch the first burn: if the pool of liquid wax does not reach the outer edge within 2 hours, the wick may be undersized for the diameter. See
for guidance on the next batch.

Store in a cool, dry place away from direct sunlight. A white bloom may develop on the beeswax surface, wax crystallisation that is normal and harmless; buff with a soft cloth to restore the sheen. Beeswax candles have no practical shelf limit.
